technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing build, benchmark, configuration, RPM, and documentation conventions rather than introducing new frameworks or tooling.
Implement the Reactor upgrade to version 2.0.3 through the project's existing dependency-management mechanism and resolve compatibility issues in dependent modules.
Make JMX disabled by default through the existing application configuration mechanism while retaining an explicit configuration override for users who need JMX.

Treat the U1 performance work as repeatable benchmark execution and comparison across Kafka 0.8.1 and 0.8.2, covering baseline, Tuple, and Serialized payloads with In-Memory Transport to HDFS, Direct Binding Transport to HDFS, and Kafka to HDFS.
Fix Gradle distribution targets without changing the intended distribution contents or introducing a replacement build system.
Support multiple XD container instances by adding instance-specific PID, log, configuration, and service/runtime handling to the existing RPM scripts.
Update documentation using the existing documentation structure, adding navigable links to out-of-the-box batch jobs and analytics widgets.
Validate the increment with focused tests plus a broader regression and packaging verification pass.
assumptions: The existing source repository, CI/build environment, benchmark harness, Kafka environments, HDFS environment, and RPM packaging definitions are available and functional enough to modify.
The benchmark infrastructure already supports the required transports and sinks; effort is limited to adapting, configuring, executing, and comparing the requested scenarios.
Kafka 0.8.1 and 0.8.2 test environments can be provisioned or accessed without developing new Kafka infrastructure.
The Reactor 2.0.3 dependency is compatible with the project's supported Java and Spring XD baseline, with only localized source or test changes required.
No new product features beyond the eight stated user stories are required.
Documentation content for batch jobs and analytics widgets can be derived from existing implementations and examples; no separate UX or technical-writing review cycle is required.
One workday represents one person-day of productive development effort, excluding waiting time for external environments or approvals.
The estimate includes implementation, developer testing, troubleshooting, and documentation updates, but excludes long-running benchmark execution time when no developer effort is required.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the project structure, existing Gradle tasks, dependency declarations, JMX configuration, RPM scripts, benchmark definitions, documentation navigation, and current test status; identify affected modules and establish a change plan.

activities.activity_name: Kafka payload and sink benchmark support
activities.activity_description: Prepare and execute repeatable comparisons for baseline, Tuple, and Serialized payloads across Kafka 0.8.1 and 0.8.2, covering In-Memory Transport to HDFS, Direct Binding Transport to HDFS, and Kafka to HDFS; correct benchmark configuration or harness issues, collect results, and produce comparison evidence.
Update dependency declarations and transitive dependency constraints, compile affected modules, resolve API or behavioral incompatibilities, and run focused unit and integration tests.

Change the default JMX setting, preserve an explicit opt-in configuration, update relevant tests and configuration documentation, and verify startup and management behavior with JMX enabled and disabled.

Diagnose and fix the local ./gradlew dist and distZip failures, verify generated artifacts and included files, and confirm that publish-build behavior remains consistent with the intended distribution layout.

Run the build with compiler and Javadoc diagnostics enabled, correct actionable source, annotation, documentation, and configuration issues, and verify that the build output is free of the targeted warnings.

activities.activity_name: RPM support for multiple XD container instances
activities.activity_description: Modify the RPM startup, shutdown, status, and configuration handling so multiple xd-container instances can run on one node with distinct instance identifiers, PID files, logs, ports or configuration locations as applicable; validate installation and lifecycle operations.

Add or correct documentation references and navigation links for out-of-the-box batch jobs, including links from the relevant overview to each job's detailed section, and verify generated or rendered documentation.

Document the analytics tab and its streaming-pipeline widgets, including widget purpose, basic usage, and relevant configuration or interpretation guidance; integrate the content into the existing documentation navigation.
Run affected unit, integration, build, documentation, RPM lifecycle, JMX, dependency, and representative XD runtime tests; investigate failures caused by the increment and make corrective changes.
Review the complete change set, update release or build metadata where required, confirm distribution artifacts and documentation outputs, and prepare the implementation for handoff or merge.
